title: What Good Commercial Cleaning Actually Looks Like (And How to Tell When It's Dropped)

body:
## Start with the agreed work, not a general impression

Good commercial cleaning is easier to assess when the areas, tasks and frequencies are written down. A workplace can look tidy while a scheduled detail task is missed. Equally, an untidy desk may sit outside a cleaner's agreed access or clear-desk arrangements.

For offices in Newcastle CBD and Lake Macquarie, use this guide to review delivery against the actual scope. It does not certify hygiene or diagnose a health risk from appearance.

## Walk the site with the task schedule

Choose a time that makes sense in relation to the cleaning visit. An observation after a busy working day tells you something different from a check immediately after service. Record when the task was due and when you looked.

Check the areas included in your agreement:

- Reception and meeting rooms: agreed surfaces, accessible glass, bins and floors.
- Work areas: accessible surfaces and floor areas, with clear-desk exclusions respected.
- Kitchens: scheduled benches, sink, bins, appliance surfaces and floors.
- Amenities: agreed fixtures, surfaces, floors and consumable responsibilities.
- Detail areas: edges, skirtings or periodic work only where included and due.

These are prompts, not default inclusions or prescribed cleaning frequencies. Use the final proposal to establish what should have happened.

## Use four findings instead of a vague score

| Finding | What it means | Next step |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Included task missed | Work was due, in scope and accessible | Raise it with the provider and agree follow-up |
| Scope mismatch | The task or frequency no longer fits workplace use | Review the schedule and price before changing expectations |
| Access prevented work | A room was occupied, restricted or obstructed | Agree practical access and record any deferred work |
| Maintenance or specialist issue | Cleaning alone may not resolve it | Refer to the responsible person or suitable specialist |

For example, an included floor edge not cleaned when due is a delivery question. A kitchen needing attention between visits may be a timing or shared-responsibility question. A leak or damaged surface needs the appropriate maintenance response.

## Keep an issue log people can act on

Record the date, area, task, observation, access circumstances, agreed action, responsible contact and review date. If a photo helps, leave people, private paperwork and screens out of the frame.

Ask the provider to confirm how an issue is raised and who follows it through. Agree response and escalation arrangements for the actual site rather than assuming every service has the same deadline. Check that the action was completed, not simply that the message was received.

Our [Workplace Cleaning Brief & Comparison Checklist (PDF)](/guides/workplace-cleaning-scope-checklist.pdf) includes an issue log and room/task schedule. It is available without an email registration.

## Review consistency without promising the same person forever

Familiarity helps a team understand access, surfaces and priorities. Absences and staffing changes still happen. Ask how site notes, scope revisions and instructions are handed over when someone changes.

A useful review covers both the work and the information behind it: are the site instructions current, do replacements receive them, and does the workplace know who to contact? A familiar face alone does not establish that every task is completed.

## What YOS makes accountable

YOS provides [commercial cleaning in Newcastle CBD and Lake Macquarie](/cleaning). Sarah oversees the cleaning relationship and monthly quality assurance against the agreed Scope of Works. We aim to keep consistent teams wherever possible, supported by documented scopes, site notes and a direct management pathway for issues.

The site inspection and written proposal establish your workplace's inclusions, service timing and arrangements. Ordinary office cleaning should not be assumed to meet specialist clinical, childcare, hazardous-material or other sector-specific requirements.

## When to review the scope

Changes to attendance, visitors, working hours, furniture or room use can change the workload. Review those circumstances with the provider and document approved changes. More visits will not automatically fix an unclear task list or a maintenance problem.

Use our [busier office scope-review guide](/blog/commercial-cleaning-scope-busier-office) if the workplace has changed. For procurement, see the [Newcastle cleaning scope and quote checklist](/blog/commercial-cleaning-newcastle-what-to-expect) and [whole-scope cost comparison](/blog/commercial-cleaning-cost-newcastle).

## Decide the next step from the evidence

Start with a specific issue and the agreed scope. That gives both parties a practical basis for correction, clarification or a change in service. If you are considering a new provider, prepare a [cleaning changeover plan](/blog/switch-commercial-cleaning-company-newcastle) so the same uncertainty does not carry into the next agreement.
